name: Rivendell
note: Fan work from Tolkien, whose work belongs to the Tolkien Estate; nothing from any book, film or game is used, and every shape here is this project's own geometry built from the description. The cleft, the moor above it, the Bruinen and the ford are generated by tools/make-rivendell.py. The point of the place is the ground: you come over open moor and it stops, and the valley is three hundred metres under your feet with the house on ledges partway down. Positions are [lat, lon] against an origin at the Last Homely House.

landmarks.name: The Last Homely House
landmarks.info: Not a palace and not a fortress: a long house of many halls on a ledge above the water, with the roofs pitched steep because this is a wet valley, the galleries facing the falls, and a fire going in it at every hour of the year. Everything about the building is about being somewhere else than the weather.

landmarks.name: The Hall of Fire
landmarks.info: The one room in the house that is never empty and never quiet: a hearth at each end, a floor for singing on, and the doors open onto the gallery over the river.

landmarks.name: The Ford of Bruinen
landmarks.info: Where the East Road crosses. The water is shallow and quick over gravel, and the valley's defence is not a wall - it is that anything coming down the road has to stand in the river to get in.

landmarks.name: The Bridge
landmarks.info: One span from the terraces to the far wall, on two piers with a pointed relieving arch in each, and no parapet worth the name in the middle of it. There are several of these; the first is the one everybody means.

landmarks.name: The upper bridge
landmarks.info: Another of the spans. The valley is crossed wherever two terraces face each other, because the only way about in it is on foot.

landmarks.name: The lower bridge
landmarks.info: Another of the spans. The valley is crossed wherever two terraces face each other, because the only way about in it is on foot.

landmarks.name: The pavilion above the fall
landmarks.info: Eight posts, a steep cone with a gilt finial on it, a seat round the inside and nothing else. There are a number of these and they are what makes the valley read as built for pleasure rather than for shelter.

landmarks.name: A stair
landmarks.info: The valley is vertical and nobody in it has a cart, so the stairs are architecture: flights of dressed stone switching back down the wall, a landing at every turn with a newel post on it, and a balustrade the whole way down the side with the drop.

landmarks.name: A figure
landmarks.info: Nothing here has a face: a massing model cannot carve one and a bad one is worse than none. What it has is the silhouette - a tall robed figure on a stepped plinth, at the head of a stair or the end of a terrace, half of them holding something up.

landmarks.name: The falls
landmarks.info: Every stream on the moor arrives over the rim, and there are a great many streams. Each one is a sheet of white that does not touch the wall again until the bottom, with a plume of mist standing at the foot of it. The noise of them is why nobody in the house speaks quietly.
